11: # Hybrid Design Tokens
12: 
13: There is **one source of truth** for design tokens in this project, and it feeds every
14: surface. Never hardcode a palette, spacing, radius, or type value twice. Never let the
15: Flutter theme and the Tailwind theme drift.
16: 
17: ## Token source → outputs
18: 
19: ```
20: assets/templates/design-tokens/tokens.toml          ← THE source. Edit only this.
21:    │  node scripts/gen-design-tokens.mjs <root>
22:    ├── desktop/src/theme.css                        Tailwind 4 @theme (+ light override)
23:    └── mobile/lib/core/theme/tokens.dart            Dart token class
24: ```
25: 
26: Both outputs carry a `GENERATED … DO NOT EDIT` banner. Edit `tokens.toml` and re-run
27: the script; never hand-edit a generated file.
28: 
29: ### Why this is generated and not "kept in sync"
30: 
31: "One token source" used to be aspiration rather than mechanism: the two files were
32: hand-mirrored, and they had **already drifted** — `#0D0D18` on Flutter against
33: `#0B0F14` on React for the same app-background role, with nothing in the build to
34: notice. Two palettes that agree on intent and disagree on values is worse than one
35: ugly palette, because every screenshot comparison becomes unreliable.
36: 
37: Generation makes the drift impossible instead of merely discouraged.
38: `theme-factory` may help explore a palette, but it is not a cross-platform token
39: compiler and must never be cited as parity proof.
40: 
41: ## Naming: role, never colour
42: 
43: A token is named for the **job it does**, never the colour it currently holds.
44: `accent` survives a rebrand; `ember` becomes a lie the first time the brand changes,
45: and renaming it then touches every call site. The generator emits deprecated
46: colour-word aliases (`red` → `danger`) only so older code keeps compiling — new code
47: uses the semantic name.
48: 
49: Group prefixes keep roles legible and prevent collisions: `bgSurface` is a
50: background, `textPrimary` is a text role. A flat namespace fights over the obvious
51: words.
52: 
53: ## Light and dark are the same names
54: 
55: Both themes define the **same token names** with different values, so no component
56: ever branches on theme — it reads a role and gets the right colour. Both must satisfy
57: WCAG 2.2 AA against their own background; changing a value is a contrast change, so
58: re-check it (`a11y-gate`).
59: 
60: ## Token categories (define once, reference everywhere)
61: 
62: - **Color** — semantic, not decorative: `canvas`, `chrome`, `surface`, `raised`, `hover`,
63:   `text`, `muted`, `accent`, `destructive`, `focus`. Provide a full light AND dark scale.
64: - **Spacing** — a scale (`space-1…space-section`), not per-component padding. Use fluid
65:   `clamp()` for section-level rhythm on web.
66: - **Typography** — at most two families with a deliberate pairing; fluid `clamp()` sizes
67:   (`text-base`, `text-hero`); `font-display: swap`; preload only the critical weight.
68: - **Radius / motion** — `radius`, `duration-*`, `ease-*`. This project is strict Flat 2.0: no
69:   visible borders/divider lines and no layout shadows. Adjacent areas differ by background.
70: 
71: ## Rules
72: 
73: 1. **No magic values in components.** Web: reference `var(--…)` / Tailwind token classes.
74:    Flutter: reference `Theme.of(context).colorScheme` / a typed `AppTokens` extension —
75:    never a raw `Color(0xFF…)` or `EdgeInsets.all(13)` at a call site.
76: 2. **Both themes must feel intentional.** Do not default to dark mode; style light AND dark
77:    deliberately and test both (see [[tauri-ui-review]], [[flutter-golden-ui]]).
78: 3. **Semantic naming wins.** Name by role (`accent`, `destructive`), never by hue
79:    (`blue`, `red`) at the token-consumption site.
80: 4. **Cross-surface parity.** The same semantic token must resolve to the same intent on
81:    web and mobile. When you change a token, regenerate BOTH outputs in the same change.
82: 5. **ContentBlock styling flows from tokens.** Every [[content-block-ui]] variant styles
83:    from these tokens — no per-variant ad-hoc colors.
